text.p: The chairman of Italy's Bishops' Conference flew to Havana on Thursday for an official three-day visit, the first time Cuba's Communist authorities have welcomed such a senior figure from the Roman Catholic church.

Church sources said Cardinal Camillo Ruini would lead a delegation to visit charitable works supported by the Italian Church and meet officials. They did not rule out that the meeting could also be a preparation for a planned visit by Pope John Paul to Cuba this year.
Cuban President Fidel Castro met the Pope, a crusader against communism, at the Vatican in November and invited him to Cuba. The Pope accepted.
Tensions between Havana and the Roman Catholic Church have eased notably in recent months and the Church hopes the new improved climate will boost its status in the Caribbean island.

Shortly after Castro took control in 1959, Cuba was declared a socialist state. Some 350 Catholic schools were nationalised and more than 100 priests expelled. Freedom of worship and religious instruction are limited to Church premises.
Ruini will travel on to Haiti on Sunday, Church sources said.
